Your first $16,600 next year? Federal income tax-free.
The IRS set the 2027 standard deduction on Nov 5: $16,600 for single filers (up $500) and $33,200 for married couples filing jointly (up $1,000).
Bracket thresholds rise an average of 3.2%; tax rates stay the same.
Our math: a single filer earning the same $60,000 owes about $68 less federal income tax.
It applies to 2027 income, on returns filed in 2028.
Sources: IRS (IR-2026-133, Rev. Proc. 2026-35), Journal of Accountancy, CPA Practice Advisor.
News and education, not financial advice.
